# [P2] Map futures delta and MOSERS workbook warning codes in data quality pipeline taxonomy

## Why

`src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:11` defines `_SEVERITY_BY_CODE` and `_CATEGORY_BY_CODE` mapping data quality warning codes to categories and severity levels. However, warning codes emitted by `src/counter_risk/compute/futures_delta.py:27` (`"NO_PRIOR_MATCH"`, `"NO_PRIOR_MONTH_MATCH"`) and `src/counter_risk/writers/mosers_workbook.py:44` (`"WRITEBACK_MISSING_DESCRIPTION"`, `"WRITEBACK_NO_WORKBOOK_MATCH"`) are omitted from both dictionaries. Consequently, `categorize_issue` in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:65` falls back to generic category `"pipeline"` and severity `"medium"` instead of domain category `"data_validation"`, skewing automated data quality reporting and issue grouping.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py`, add `"NO_PRIOR_MATCH"`, `"NO_PRIOR_MONTH_MATCH"`, `"WRITEBACK_MISSING_DESCRIPTION"`, and `"WRITEBACK_NO_WORKBOOK_MATCH"` to `_SEVERITY_BY_CODE` and `_CATEGORY_BY_CODE`, and add regression tests in `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to data quality pipeline interfaces. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py`, register `"NO_PRIOR_MATCH"`, `"NO_PRIOR_MONTH_MATCH"`, `"WRITEBACK_MISSING_DESCRIPTION"`, and `"WRITEBACK_NO_WORKBOOK_MATCH"` in `_SEVERITY_BY_CODE` and `_CATEGORY_BY_CODE`.
- [ ] In `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py`, add tests verifying `categorize_issue` returns `"data_validation"` for these warning codes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py -q` passes; newly registered warning codes map to `"data_validation"`.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies `categorize_issue("NO_PRIOR_MATCH")` returns category `"data_validation"`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break mapping in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py` by removing `"NO_PRIOR_MATCH"`; taxonomy mapping test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

Explicitly mapping pipeline warning codes ensures consistent categorization in downstream audit and data quality summary dashboards.
issues.title: [P2] Map futures delta and MOSERS workbook warning codes in data quality pipeline taxonomy

# [P2] Format non-finite floats and None defensively in PPT concentration table slides

## Why

`src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py:86` formats metric cell values in `append_concentration_table_slide` using `f"{float(value):.2%}"` without checking `math.isfinite()`, and without handling `None` values. When metric values contain `None`, `nan`, or `inf`, PPT table slides render raw strings like `"None"`, `"nan%"`, or `"inf%"` into presentation slide cells. In contrast, other PPT report renderers in the codebase format missing or non-finite values as `"-"` or `"N/A"`.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py`, add defensive formatting for `None`, non-numeric, and non-finite (`nan`, `inf`) values to render placeholder strings (e.g. `"-"` or `"N/A"`), and add regression tests in `tests/ppt/test_concentration_table.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to slide layout or python-pptx shape hierarchy. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py`, safely format percentage and numeric values in `append_concentration_table_slide` when encountering `None`, `NaN`, `Inf`, or invalid values.
- [ ] In `tests/ppt/test_concentration_table.py`, add unit tests verifying slides render placeholder strings instead of `"nan%"` or `"inf%"` when metrics contain non-finite numbers or `None`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/ppt/test_concentration_table.py -q` passes; non-finite floats and `None` values render placeholder strings in table cells.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies rendered slide table cells for `float('nan')` contain `"-"` or `"N/A"`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break non-finite handling in `src/counter_risk/ppt/concentration_table.py` by reverting to `f"{float(value):.2%}"`; non-finite PPT test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

Sanitizing float representations prevents presentation decks from displaying raw floating point artifacts to executives.
issues.title: [P2] Format non-finite floats and None defensively in PPT concentration table slides

# [P2] Reject boolean values in XLSX reader accounting float coercion

## Why

`src/counter_risk/parsers/_xlsx_reader.py:171` implements `coerce_accounting_float(value)`. In Python, `isinstance(True, (int, float))` evaluates to `True`. Because `coerce_accounting_float` lacks an explicit `isinstance(value, bool)` check before checking `isinstance(value, (int, float))`, boolean values are converted to numeric floats (`coerce_accounting_float(True) == 1.0`, `coerce_accounting_float(False) == 0.0`) instead of raising `ValueError`. This causes accidental boolean flags in Excel workbook cells to be parsed as numerical dollar/notional amounts.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/parsers/_xlsx_reader.py`, add `if isinstance(value, bool): raise ValueError(...)` guard at the top of `coerce_accounting_float`, and add unit tests in `tests/parsers/test_numeric.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to regex-based accounting string parsing. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/parsers/_xlsx_reader.py`, add explicit boolean rejection to `coerce_accounting_float`.
- [ ] In `tests/parsers/test_numeric.py`, add unit tests verifying `coerce_accounting_float(True)` and `coerce_accounting_float(False)` raise `ValueError`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/parsers/test_numeric.py -q` passes; boolean values raise `ValueError` on coercion.
- [ ] Direct inspection confirms `coerce_accounting_float(True)` raises `ValueError`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break `coerce_accounting_float` in `src/counter_risk/parsers/_xlsx_reader.py` by removing the boolean check; boolean test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

An explicit `isinstance(value, bool)` check prevents `bool` subclasses of `int` from bypassing validation.
issues.title: [P2] Reject boolean values in XLSX reader accounting float coercion

# [P2] Support fallback keys when earlier candidates contain None in limits notional extraction

## Why

`src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py:99` implements `_find_notional(row)`. When inspecting candidate keys in `_NOTIONAL_KEYS` (`("notional", "exposure", "amount", "value", "balance", "total")`), if a row contains a key such as `"notional": None` or `"notional": ""`, line 107 immediately raises `ValueError` instead of falling through to subsequent candidate keys such as `"exposure": 500000.0`. In contrast, if the key is absent from the dict, it proceeds to the next candidate. Having a key present with `None` or empty value should continue searching fallback keys. Furthermore, `_find_notional` does not reject boolean values `True`/`False`.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py`, update `_find_notional` to fall through when a candidate key has a `None` or empty value, reject boolean values, and add unit tests in `tests/compute/test_limits.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to limit calculation logic. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py`, update `_find_notional` to continue checking remaining candidate keys when a candidate key is `None` or empty.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py`, add boolean type guard `not isinstance(val, bool)` in `_find_notional`.
- [ ] In `tests/compute/test_limits.py`, add unit tests covering candidate fallthrough for `{"notional": None, "exposure": 250000.0}` and boolean input rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/compute/test_limits.py -q` passes; fallback keys are evaluated when first key is `None` or empty.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies `_find_notional({"notional": None, "exposure": 250000.0}) == 250000.0`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break `_find_notional` in `src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py` to raise on `None` without checking fallback keys; test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

Aligns `_find_notional` fallback key traversal behavior across sparse dictionary rows containing `None` values.
issues.title: [P2] Support fallback keys when earlier candidates contain None in limits notional extraction

# [P2] Fix premature loop termination and reject booleans in rollup numeric field extraction

## Why

`src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py:106` implements `_find_numeric(row, candidates, ...)`. At line 119, when a row contains a candidate key whose value is `None` or whitespace, the loop executes `break` instead of `continue`. As a result, candidate traversal halts prematurely and raises a `ValueError` even when valid fallback candidate keys exist in `candidates` (e.g., `{"notional": None, "exposure": 100.0}` with candidates `("notional", "exposure")` raises `ValueError: Missing required numeric field` instead of returning `100.0`). Additionally, `_find_numeric` does not check `isinstance(val, bool)`, allowing `True` to coerce to `1.0`.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, change `break` to `continue` when candidate value is `None` or empty string, add `isinstance(val, bool)` check to reject booleans, and add unit tests in `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to rollup aggregation algorithms. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, change `break` to `continue` in `_find_numeric` when candidate value is `None` or empty.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, reject boolean values in `_find_numeric`.
- [ ] In `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`, add tests verifying alias fallthrough when earlier candidate keys have `None` or empty string values, and verifying boolean inputs raise `ValueError`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/compute/test_rollups.py -q` passes; candidate keys fall through properly on `None` values.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies `_find_numeric({"notional": None, "exposure": 100.0}, ("notional", "exposure")) == 100.0`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break `_find_numeric` by putting `break` back in `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`; the alias fallback test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

Using `continue` allows dictionary records with explicit `None` entries in primary column fields to resolve through valid backup alias columns.
issues.title: [P2] Fix premature loop termination and reject booleans in rollup numeric field extraction

# [P2] Fix alias fallthrough and reject booleans in change attribution float parsing

## Why

`src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py:96` defines `_optional_float(row, keys)`. When iterating through fallback candidate keys in `keys` (e.g. `_DELTA_COLUMNS` at `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py:35`), if the first matching key contains `None` or an empty string, line 108 executes `return None` immediately instead of continuing the loop to check subsequent alias keys (e.g. `{"delta": None, "daily_change": 42.5}` returns `None` instead of `42.5`). Furthermore, `_optional_float` and `_first_float` at `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py:84` do not guard against `isinstance(raw, bool)` or non-finite values, allowing booleans like `True` to coerce to `1.0`.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py`, update `_optional_float` to continue to subsequent fallback keys when a candidate key is `None`, empty, or invalid, and add `not isinstance(raw, bool)` and `math.isfinite()` guards to `_first_float` and `_optional_float`. Add unit tests in `tests/test_change_attribution_report.py`.

## Non-Goals

No changes to mathematical attribution models. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py`, fix `_optional_float` to iterate all candidate keys when early keys contain `None` or invalid values.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py`, ensure `_first_float` and `_optional_float` reject boolean values and non-finite floats.
- [ ] In `tests/test_change_attribution_report.py`, add unit tests covering alias key fallthrough with `None` values and boolean rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/test_change_attribution_report.py -q` passes; fallback keys are traversed when first key is `None`, and booleans raise or are rejected.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies `_optional_float({"delta": None, "daily_change": 42.5}, ("delta", "daily_change")) == 42.5`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break alias loop by restoring `return None` on first missing value in `src/counter_risk/reports/change_attribution.py`; fallback tests must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

Continuing the candidate loop on `None` or invalid values allows fallback column aliases in `_DELTA_COLUMNS` and `_PERCENT_COLUMNS` to function as intended.
issues.title: [P2] Fix alias fallthrough and reject booleans in change attribution float parsing

# [P2] Right-align numeric data cells under right-aligned column headers in pure-Python table PNG renderer

## Why

`src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py:293` defines cell text rendering in `_render_cprs_table_png`, but draws all cell text with `x + _CELL_PADDING_X` (left alignment), ignoring `column.header_align`. For columns like `"Cash"`, `"TIPS"`, `"Treasury"`, `"Equity"`, `"Commodity"`, `"Currency"`, `"Notional"`, `_DEFAULT_COLUMNS` in `src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py:75` specifies `header_align="right"`. Header text is properly right-aligned via `x + col_width - _CELL_PADDING_X - _text_width(column.name)` at `src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py:257`, but data rows under those headers remain left-aligned, causing column headers and values to be misaligned in generated PNG table reports.

## Scope

In `src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py`, calculate cell text X position based on `column.header_align == "right"` using `x + col_width - _CELL_PADDING_X - _text_width(cell_text)`, and add regression tests in `tests/renderers/test_table_png.py`.

## Non-Goals

No external image libraries or canvas alterations. Scaffold-only or partial completion does NOT count as done; the behavior and test gates must be delivered.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py`, update `_render_cprs_table_png` to position cell text using `x + col_width - _CELL_PADDING_X - _text_width(cell_text)` when `column.header_align == "right"`.
- [ ] In `tests/renderers/test_table_png.py`, add unit tests asserting right-aligned columns render text offset from the right cell boundary.
- [ ] In `tests/renderers/test_table_png.py`, add regression tests asserting rendered table PNG images align numeric data cells with right-aligned headers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/renderers/test_table_png.py -q` passes; numeric cells under right-aligned headers render right-aligned.
- [ ] Direct inspection verifies cell text X coordinates for right-aligned columns match the right-padding calculation.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: deliberately break cell alignment by reverting right-aligned calculation to `x + _CELL_PADDING_X` in `src/counter_risk/renderers/table_png.py`; the right-align test must fail; restore and rerun.

## Implementation Notes

`column.header_align` holds alignment string values like `"left"` or `"right"`. Aligning data cells under right-aligned column headers ensures numeric amounts align with header titles.
issues.title: [P2] Right-align numeric data cells under right-aligned column headers in pure-Python table PNG renderer
